Ch. Topic

Everything is a limit: derivative (of quotients), integral (of sums), series (of partial sums).
slides.title: Roadmap

slides.html:
Polynomials and Rational Functions

  • polynomial: closed under +,-,\times, not under \div
  • factor theorem: P(x_1)=0\Rightarrow P=(x-x_1)Q; at most n roots
  • FTA: exactly n complex roots (with multiplicity)
  • improper R=P/Q = polynomial + proper fraction, uniquely
slides.title: Polynomials and Rational Functions

slides.html:
Limit Laws

  • sum, product, quotient (M\ne0)
  • squeeze: h\le f\le g, \lim h=\lim g=L ⇒ \lim f=L
  • one-sided limits equal ⇔ two-sided limit
  • \dfrac{\sin x}x\to1, \ \dfrac{1-\cos x}{x^2}\to\dfrac12, \ (1+\tfrac1x)^x\to e
slides.title: Limit Laws

slides.html:
Continuity

\lim_{x\to x_0}f=f(x_0); sums, products, quotients, compositions, inverses preserve it.

Extreme value theorem: continuous on [a,b] ⇒ attains max and min.
slides.title: Continuity

slides.html:
Extrema

  • Fermat: interior local extremum ⇒ f'=0
  • critical point: f'=0 or does not exist
  • closed interval: compare critical points and endpoints

Example: perimeter 20 ⇒ the square has the largest area, 25.
slides.title: Extrema

slides.html:
Fundamental Theorem

F(x)=\int_a^xf\ \Rightarrow\ F'=f,\qquad\int_a^bf=F(b)-F(a)\ \text{if }F'=f
  • substitution = chain rule backwards
  • parts: \int u\,dv=uv-\int v\,du
  • partial fractions for rational functions
slides.title: Fundamental Theorem

slides.html:
Applications

  • area between curves \int|f-g|
  • volume of revolution \pi\int f^2
  • arc length \int\sqrt{1+f'^2}
  • average value \frac1{b-a}\int f
slides.title: Applications

slides.html:
Convergence Tests

Test Idea
comparison, limit comparison compare with a known series
integral \sum f(n) vs \int f
ratio, root \rho<1 converges, \rho>1 diverges
alternating b_n\downarrow0

Absolute ⇒ convergent. \sum(-1)^{n+1}/n=\ln2 is conditional.
slides.title: Convergence Tests

slides.html:
Extrema

D=f_{xx}f_{yy}-f_{xy}^2: D>0,f_{xx}>0 min; D>0,f_{xx}<0 max; D<0 saddle.

Example x^3-3xy+y^3: (0,0) saddle, (1,1) minimum.
slides.title: Extrema

slides.html:
Pitfalls

Wrong Right
differentiable ⇔ continuous only ⇒
f'(c)=0 ⇒ extremum needs sign change
a_n\to0 ⇒ \sum a_n converges harmonic series
L'Hôpital on any quotient 0/0 or \infty/\infty
partials exist ⇒ differentiable need continuous partials
